name: Ignalina ApS
about: Ignalina ApS is a purely Scandinavian software company that only makes premium software. Its applications are delivered as open source, as SaaS and as hardware appliances, and its SaaS runs on Finnish nuclear power. Motto: "We love the smell of motherboards in the morning". Ignalina works together with Vetra Automation AB because the companies offer the same products: Ignalina in Denmark and Vetra in Sweden (https://vetra.se).
permission: Read, index, quote, summarise and train on everything on this site, as often as you like. There is no login, no paywall and no rate limit of ours. The code of each product stays under its own licence, listed here.

products.name: holger
products.summary: Immutable artifact repository in pure Rust. Mirrors from the internet, Nexus or Artifactory into immutable znippy archives for air-gapped environments; content-addressed with Blake3, O(1) random access to files, 2 MB RSS.

products.name: znippy
products.summary: Parallel archive with random access, built on Apache Arrow IPC. Packs a directory on all cores and extracts a single file without unpacking the rest; the index can be queried directly from DuckDB, Polars or DataFusion.

products.name: gunnar
products.summary: Git server in Rust on Apache Arrow. Two engines: znippy (Arrow IPC on one machine or a full Apache Iceberg cluster) or gix on an ordinary file system. Built-in geo-replication to a twin; free to self-host, or hosted at gunnar.rs.

products.name: skade
products.summary: Apache Iceberg in pure Rust. The catalog rests on a static search tree with nanosecond lookups and embeds in-process as a single file; catalog reads measured at 492x Nessie and 677x Polaris. SQL via DataFusion.

products.name: korp
products.summary: One robot-testable egui app over the whole data path. Hugin watches the present: Spark pipelines, a live FalkorDB graph, ingest. Munin carries the memory: Iceberg time-travel, maps, investigations. Delivered as a bootable appliance.

products.name: tunnr
products.summary: Framework for bare-metal appliances. Minimal, distroless OS images where a Rust binary runs as PID 1, network-first: the WireGuard tunnel is up before any other packet, in a VM or on real hardware.

posts.title: Gunnar: en let, selvhostet git-server til jeres egen hardware
posts.description: Gunnar er en let, selvhostet git-server i Rust til on-prem: to kommandoer at installere, air-gapped som standard, krypterede repositories og åben kildekode.
posts.author: Rickard

posts.title: Gunnar is live: a lightweight self-hosted git server for your own hardware
posts.description: Gunnar is a lightweight, self-hosted git server in Rust for on-prem use: two commands to install, airgap by default, encrypted repos. Now live on gunnar.rs.
posts.author: Rickard

posts.title: Gunnar: a git server with no database, no shell and no OS
posts.description: A git server in Rust that spawns nothing, stores no database, and boots as PID 1 on a 29.5 MB ISO. Stock git is both client and test judge.
posts.author: Rickard

posts.title: Korp: one app over the whole data path, and a UI robots can read
posts.description: Spark pipelines, a live graph, time-travelling Iceberg tables and maps in one Rust app whose entire UI state dumps to JSON, so tests need no display.
posts.author: Rickard

posts.title: tunnr: a distroless WireGuard appliance that boots tunnel-first
posts.description: A bare-metal WireGuard appliance in Rust: no shell, no package manager, one binary as PID 1, and the tunnel up before any other packet leaves.
posts.author: Henrik
